thread:
Ellen (Support): FYI customer acct-8432 on dedicated-eu-west-1-8 seeing intermittent 429s + huge p99 spikes after yesterday's runtime tweak. Started ~08:15 UTC.

Ellen (Support): Examples from their app logs:
```
2026-03-17T08:22:11Z ERROR request_id=abc123 status=429 reason=capacity_exceeded queue_len=42 target_pool=dedicated-eu-west-1-8
2026-03-17T08:23:02Z WARN request_id=def456 latency=3100ms model=redwood-7b-instruct
```

Ellen (Support): Customer says these are correlated with other tenants' heavy usage windows. Asking whether this looks like noisy-neighbor GPU contention.

Rajesh (Eng-Infra): Can you paste the pool/node name and the tenant allocation? also any recent MIG / partitioning changes?

Ellen (Support): pool: dedicated-eu-west-1-8, reported node: gpu-node-47, tenant: acct-8432. We didn't change MIG config on their side.

infra-bot: Autoscaler event: pool=dedicated-eu-west-1-8 action=scale_up from=2 to=3 reason=queue_length>30 at=2026-03-17T08:20:00Z

Lucy (SRE): Pulled metrics for gpu-node-47 around spike window:
```
-p99 latency (tenant acct-8432): baseline 450ms -> spikes 2.8-3.2s
-GPU SM util: 95-99% during spikes
-Kernel run queue length: avg 38
-GPU memory used: 12.1GB / 24GB
```

Lucy (SRE): nvidia-smi snapshot:
```
GPU 0: A100-SXM4 (UUID: GPU-xxxx)
  MIG profiles present: 1g.10gb x2, 2g.20gb x1
  Processes: tenant-acct-8432(pid 1245)  + tenant-acct-7782(pid 2233)  + system
```

Rajesh (Eng-Infra): That looks like multiple MIG slices with >1 tenant on the same GPU. If one tenant saturates SMs + PCIe transfers you'll see downstream tenants get 429s when the request queue backs up.

Mike (Eng-Runtime): Agreed. Also check kernel metrics for context-switches and MPS (if enabled). Did we enable CUDA MPS? that can amplify interference.

Ellen (Support): Not sure about MPS on this cluster. Customer doesn't control host-level MPS.

Lucy (SRE): Quick repro suggestion (internal): run a synthetic load that mimics their traffic: concurrent 40 requests, seq_len=512, batching off.
```bash
# simple load loop to reproduce p99 spikes
for i in {1..40}; do 
  curl -s -X POST https://dedicated-eu-west-1-8.redwood/v1/generate -d '{"model":"redwood-7b-instruct","input":"x"*512}' &
done
```

Mike (Eng-Runtime): Also try our stress script which sets request headers to avoid client-side batching and forces per-request KV refill. (I'll DM the script).

Rajesh (Eng-Infra): Mitigation options:
- short term: move acct-8432 to an isolated node (nodeAffinity + taint)
- medium: enforce "single-mig-per-tenant" scheduling policy for pools with small MIG slices
- long term: change autoscaler trigger to scale earlier by lowering GPU util threshold (e.g., from 80% -> 60%) and reduce burst packing on the scheduler

Lucy (SRE): For immediate mitigation we can patch their deployment with nodeSelector to isolate. Example patch:
```bash
kubectl patch deployment acct-8432-runtime -n dedicated --patch '{"spec":{"template":{"spec":{"nodeSelector":{"redwood/tenant-isolation":"acct-8432"}}}}}'
```

Ellen (Support): Customer asked for a non-disruptive fix first — can we live-migrate pods?

Rajesh (Eng-Infra): We can cordon gpu-node-47 and drain non-critical pods, that will cause scheduler to reschedule onto a different node. Steps:
```bash
kubectl cordon gpu-node-47
kubectl drain gpu-node-47 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data
```
Note: draining will briefly increase latency while pods restart, but should reduce contention quickly.

Mike (Eng-Runtime): Also check the dedicated pool config — I see autoscaler.min=2 but burst cap is set to allow high pod density on each node. For noisy-tenant workloads we should lower pod_density_limit.

Ellen (Support): I can propose the cordon+drain as an immediate ops action with customer's approval. Should we open an internal incident?

Lucy (SRE): Please do. I'll own post-mortem and metric collection. We should capture: SM util, kernel queue, per-tenant request queues, and allocation mapping (which MIG slice -> tenant).

Rajesh (Eng-Infra): I'll also push a short-term scheduler tweak: prefer isolation label for tenants flagged as "latency-sensitive". That will take ~30min to roll.

Ellen (Support): Customer ok'd cordon+drain, asking for ETA.

Lucy (SRE): ETA ~10-15m to cordon+drain and verify. I'll monitor p99 and queue_len.

infra-bot: Incident created INC-2026 assigned to eng-runtime; priority=P2

Mike (Eng-Runtime): After we stabilize, let's add an automated probe: every 5m run a small 10qps probe per-tenant that records p50/p95/p99 and flags >2x baseline. That'll let autoscaler react earlier.

Ellen (Support): Noted, I updated the customer. Will paste follow-up once Lucy confirms metrics. :thumbsup:

Lucy (SRE): Post-drain quick check (08:38 UTC): p99 for acct-8432 back to ~470ms, queue_len < 5, no 429s observed for 10m. Continuing to monitor.

Ellen (Support): Thanks team — keeping INC-2026 open until we have a scheduler-level mitigation and a short writeup for the customer.

Rajesh (Eng-Infra): Follow-ups: 1) schedule policy change to avoid colocating high-throughput tenants on same MIG slice 2) propose autoscaler threshold change 3) add a tenant isolation toggle in console. I'll wire these into backlog items.

Mike (Eng-Runtime): I'll send the repro harness + recommended probe config in the incident ticket.

Ellen (Support): Closing the immediate loop with customer, will post final note in INC-2026 when we have a long-term plan. :white_check_mark:
